title: Who can apply (ukri.org)
text:
You can only apply for this funding opportunity if we have invited you to do so following a successful Gambling Harms Research and Innovation Partnerships phase one application.
This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
Who is eligible to apply
Research teams that have received Gambling Harms Research and Innovation Partnership phase one funding. These teams can change their team structure and co-leads, but the project lead must be the same as the phase one lead.
Further eligibility requirements
Lived experience and diversity
Applications must be team based and must bring together diverse people, expertise, experiences, places, and wider stakeholders. This includes people with lived and learned experience from gambling and gambling related harms.
By lived experience, we mean people with direct experience of gambling related harms.
Applicants should demonstrate how people with living and lived experience of gambling have been involved in preparing the funding application and will be involved in the research going forwards in a way that is meaningful, planned, appropriately resourced, and integrated throughout, rather than an add-on. Please explain:
how people with experience of gambling and any relevant community members have shaped the proposal so far
who will be involved and what their roles will be going forwards
how involvement will influence different stages of the research lifecycle
how the needs and lived experiences of diverse communities will be reflected
how you will evaluate the impact of involving people with experience of gambling and relevant community members
an appropriate, costed budget for involvement
who will lead this within the research team
For this funding opportunity, you have the option of costing the Gambling Harms Research UK Evidence Centre’s Addictions Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement (APPIE) network into the application. This is not a requirement. If costed into the application, the APPIE network hub can organise and host meetings, take meeting minutes, facilitate smooth payments, ensure robust communications between researchers and lived experience collaborators, and assist with evaluating the impact of involvement and engagement. These will be discussed on a case-by-case basis as you prepare your application.
Partners and collaborations
We would expect all Research and Innovation Partnerships to be multi-institutional. Partnerships with non-academic higher education institutions and people across the third sector, community groups, industry, the public sector, people with lived experience and the public are important. These kinds of collaborations can strengthen the diversity, innovation, and potential for impact from research activities. However, teams should be aware of any perceived or real potential conflict of interests within proposed partnerships. This particularly applies to partnerships with industry, including the gambling industry.
Collaborations can take different forms including project partners or collaborating organisations. You must demonstrate how the collaborations within your team are equitable, have contributed to the development of your application including its conceptualisation, and will help the centre achieve its aims. In addition, you must show how collaborations are not compromised by non-compliance with our conflict of interest policy . By ‘industry’ we mean any enterprise that places goods or services on a market and whose commercial activities constitute more than 20% of its annual operations. This definition applies across all sectors and is not limited to organisations within the gambling industry. However, there are sensitivities with respect to partnerships with businesses, the gambling industry or otherwise, meaning additional care should be taken to manage risks and avoid potential conflicts of interest.
For this opportunity, the Gambling Harms Research Network definition of the gambling industry applies. That definition is ‘By gambling industry we mean organisations and entities that design, manufacture, prepare for sale, supply data or insight to produce, distribute, market, promote or sell gambling products (including lotteries). This includes B-2-C (business to consumer) as well as B-2-B (business to business) companies.’
Conflicts of interest
UKRI does not permit funding to be provided to Gambling Commission licence holders who are subject to the levy. Co-funding from Gambling Commission license holder is not permitted. Furthermore, UKRI would not expect individual researchers to concurrently hold funding from licence holders subject to the levy or other members of the gambling industry while receiving funding from the UKRI Research Programme on Gambling.
Any engagement with industry partners, especially those from the gambling sector, must adhere to UKRI policies on the management of conflict of interests. UKRI does not permit engagement with industries whose core business can be associated with harm to public health or societal wellbeing, in line with our ethical standards and harms-based exclusion principles. This includes the gambling industry. Exceptions may be made for time-limited, purpose-specific interactions deemed essential to achieving legitimate and high-quality research objectives (for example, access to proprietary datasets or materials), provided that:
there is no direct funding or co-authorship from the excluded entity
the interaction is subject to robust ethical review and declared transparently
appropriate safeguards are in place to prevent undue influence, reputational risk, or conflicts of interest
the public benefit of the research demonstrably outweighs the risks of engagement
Such exceptions must be approved in advance through UKRI’s due diligence and governance mechanisms. Please discuss any issues arising with UKRI prior to submission of an application via the UKRI RPG inbox RPGinfo@ahrc.ukri.org . You should consider UKRI’s policies and guidance on Preventing harm in research when preparing applications to this funding opportunity.
You should declare in the declaration of interest section of your application that you are compliant with these requirements for the duration of the programme. Applicants may wish to review the Gambling Harms Research UK Network Disclosure of Interest Policy (PDF, 417KB) for further guidance.
All applications will be subject to robust scrutiny through our expert review and governance processes. Particular attention will be paid to the independence and integrity of the research, the source and independence of the findings, and the potential for real-world impact in understanding gambling behaviour and reducing gambling harms.
Any engagement with industry partners, especially those from the gambling sector, must be demonstrably independent, evidence-based and research-led. Engagement must align with the programme’s public interest objectives to further understanding of gambling-related harms and should be discussed with UKRI prior to submission of an application via the UKRI RPG inbox RPGinfo@ahrc.ukri.org

Particular attention will be paid to the independence and integrity of the research, the source and independence of the findings, and the potential for real-world impact in understanding gambling behaviour and reducing gambling harms.
UKRI wishes to clarify that, as well as not being permitted to host awards, under the Research Programme on Gambling, UKRI does not permit funding to be provided to Gambling Commission licence holders who are subject to the levy.
Early and mid-career researchers
We recognise that it is likely the successful application will be led by experienced researchers who are internationally recognised, with proven ability to deliver a large-scale project successfully and lead an investment of this nature. However, you should carefully consider the balance of your proposed teams to ensure there is a mix of people with varied expertise and at different career stages.
Your core team must include early career researchers and have clear plans for their development.
International researchers
UKRI’s international project co-lead policy applies to this funding opportunity. If you are a researcher based outside of the UK, you can be named as ‘project co-lead (international)’ if you meet the eligibility criteria for international project co-leads.
The U research organisation which hosts the project lead will be responsible for the due diligence and confirming that any international organisation and project co-lead meets the eligibility criteria. Further information on the eligibility criteria for international research organisations is provided in the UKRI project co-lead (international) policy and guidance .
